cards.front: What does the point system record, and what can repeated convictions cause?
cards.back: The DMV point system identifies and controls problem drivers by recording every traffic conviction with its date, nature and court, assigning points to in-state and out-of-state moving violations by seriousness, and repeated convictions can build a record that leads to suspension.

cards.front: How long do points stay on your record?
cards.back: Points remain on your driving record for two years from the conviction date.

cards.front: What happens at six points and at twelve points?
cards.back: At six or more points the DMV sends a letter of caution urging careful and lawful driving, and at twelve points your driver's license is subject to suspension.

cards.front: How can you remove three points, and what are the limits?
cards.back: Completing an approved eight-hour defensive driving class removes three points, but only once every twelve months, only for courses the DMV approves, and not if the class is taken without approval or before the points appear on the record.

cards.front: How many points does fleeing from an officer carry?
cards.back: Fleeing from an officer carries eight points, the highest value on the point scale.

cards.front: Which offenses carry six points?
cards.back: Six points are assessed for speeding in a school zone, reckless driving, hit and run meaning leaving the scene or failing to reveal identity, and speeding twenty miles per hour or more over the limit.

cards.front: How many points do the two lower speeding tiers carry?
cards.back: Speeding fifteen to nineteen miles per hour over the limit carries five points, while speeding eleven to fourteen miles per hour over carries three points.

cards.front: Which device, passing, yield, signal and control offenses carry three points?
cards.back: Three points are assessed for three or more wireless communication device violations, a passing violation, failure to yield, failure to obey a traffic light or a stop sign, hazardous driving, driving left of center, driving too fast for conditions and failure to maintain control of the vehicle.

cards.front: Which careless, wrong-way, littering and lane offenses carry three points?
cards.back: Three points also apply to careless or hazardous driving, driving the wrong way on a one-way street, littering, an improper lane violation, failure to observe a safety zone, failure to follow a police officer's instructions and driving on the wrong side of the road.

cards.front: Which offenses carry two points?
cards.back: Two points are assessed for following too closely, more than three passengers in the front seat, improper turning, improper backing, an improper signal or no signal, and every other moving violation not listed on the scale.

cards.front: What differs between six points and twelve points on the record?
cards.back: Six points on the record bring only a letter of caution, whereas twelve points make the license subject to suspension.

cards.front: How does the defensive driving deduction compare with how long points last?
cards.back: The approved defensive driving class removes three points and may be used once every twelve months, while points themselves stay on the record for two years from conviction.

cards.front: How do points climb with speed over the limit?
cards.back: The speeding point tiers climb from three points for eleven to fourteen miles per hour over, to five points for fifteen to nineteen over, to six points for twenty or more over the limit.

cards.front: Which offense carries the most points and which carry the fewest?
cards.back: Fleeing from an officer is the only eight-point offense on the scale, while following too closely and improper turning sit at the bottom with two points.

cards.front: What happens if your vehicle was uninsured on the day of a crash?
cards.back: If your vehicle was not covered by the required West Virginia liability insurance on the date of a crash, your vehicle registration and your driving privilege will be suspended.

cards.front: What liability insurance requirement applies to motorists on West Virginia public roads?
cards.back: Every motorist driving on West Virginia public roads is required by state law to carry West Virginia motor vehicle liability insurance meeting the minimum coverage set by law.

cards.front: What insurance duty comes with registration, and what if coverage is cancelled?
cards.back: When you obtain or renew a vehicle registration you must prove West Virginia liability insurance and keep it for the full registration year, and if the insurance is cancelled for any reason you must surrender the registration plate to the DMV.

cards.front: What proof of insurance must be in the vehicle, and when must you show it?
cards.back: A certificate of insurance or other proof of West Virginia liability insurance must be carried in the vehicle at all times with a valid registration card, an image on a wireless communication device counts as valid proof, and you must present the proof to an investigating officer after a crash and at any vehicle inspection.

cards.front: How does the DMV check insurance, and what happens without proof?
cards.back: The DMV may verify insurance at any time during the registration year, including directly and electronically with insurance companies, and failing to provide proof of West Virginia liability insurance suspends both the driver's license and the vehicle registration with reinstatement or penalty fees.

cards.front: What follows a ticket or crash report showing no insurance?
cards.back: A ticket or crash report showing no West Virginia liability insurance can suspend your license and registration plate, repeat offenses lengthen the license suspension, and reinstatement requires current proof of insurance plus mandatory reinstatement fees.

cards.front: What are the penalties for filing false insurance information?
cards.back: Filing false or fraudulent insurance information brings an additional ninety-day license suspension, revocation of the vehicle registration, and possible prosecution carrying a fine of not more than one thousand dollars and jail time of not more than one year.

cards.front: Which three loss categories are covered by West Virginia minimum liability insurance?
cards.back: State law sets minimum liability coverage categories for one death or injury, for two deaths or injuries, and for property damage.

cards.front: When may an electronic communications device be used while driving?
cards.back: Using any electronic communications device while driving on a public street or highway is prohibited unless the use is accomplished with hands-free equipment, and the handbook notes that a driver's concentration drops twenty to thirty-three percent when using a wireless device.

cards.front: What is a hands-free device, and which devices does the law cover?
cards.back: A hands-free device has a feature that lets the user engage it without either or both hands, and electronic communications devices include cell phones, personal digital assistants, mobile data devices, laptops, pagers, broadband personal communication devices, two-way messaging devices, electronic games and portable computers.

cards.front: Which uses of a handheld device while driving break the law?
cards.back: Using a device that is not hands-free to make a call, view or transmit images or data, play games, or compose, send, read, view, access, browse, transmit, save or retrieve e-mail, text messages or other electronic data violates the law.

cards.front: What are the fines and points for first, second and later device offenses?
cards.back: The electronic-device fines are one hundred dollars and zero points for a first offense, two hundred dollars and zero points for a second offense, and three hundred dollars and three points for a third or later offense.

cards.front: Which emergency and official uses are not violations of the device law?
cards.back: Using an electronic communications device to report a fire, traffic crash, serious road hazard or emergency to the authorities is not a violation, and neither is use by a law-enforcement officer, firefighter, emergency medical technician, paramedic or authorized emergency vehicle operator performing official duties.

cards.front: When do points first attach to an electronic-device offense?
cards.back: The first and second electronic-device offenses carry rising fines but zero points, and only the third and later offenses add three points to the record.

cards.front: What device use is allowed while driving, and what is a violation?
cards.back: Hands-free use of an electronic device is allowed while driving, but any call, image, game or message handled on a device that is not hands-free is a violation.

decks.module: Mandatory revocation and driving while suspended

cards.front: Which convictions involving homicide, graduated drivers, false information or leaving a crash require revocation?
cards.back: The DMV must revoke a license upon final conviction of manslaughter or negligent homicide from operating a motor vehicle, two or more moving violations as a graduated driver, providing false information to the DMV, or leaving the scene of a crash that results in death or personal injury.

cards.front: Which reckless driving, racing, suspended driving and judgment failures require revocation?
cards.back: Mandatory revocation also follows three reckless driving convictions within twenty-four months, racing on streets or highways, driving while suspended or revoked, and failing to satisfy a civil judgment arising from an automobile crash.

cards.front: Which DUI, gasoline theft and felony convictions require revocation?
cards.back: Mandatory revocation further follows a conviction in any state for driving under the influence of alcohol, controlled substances or drugs, a second conviction for failing to pay for gasoline, and any felony committed using a motor vehicle.

cards.front: What are the penalties for driving while suspended or while revoked for DUI?
cards.back: Driving while your license is suspended or revoked for a non-DUI reason may cause a ninety-day suspension, while driving while revoked for DUI carries a mandatory minimum jail sentence of thirty days to six months and a further six-month revocation of the driving privilege.

cards.front: Which license frauds are illegal, and what is the penalty?
cards.back: Giving false information on any license application is illegal, as is using someone else's license, letting another person use yours, letting someone use your identity documents to get a license, or displaying a fictitious license, and the penalty is a ninety-day suspension.

cards.front: How do penalties differ for driving while suspended and driving while revoked for DUI?
cards.back: Driving while suspended for a non-DUI reason may bring a ninety-day suspension, whereas driving while revoked for DUI brings mandatory jail of thirty days to six months plus a six-month revocation.

cards.front: Which revocation triggers depend on a count within a time window?
cards.back: Mandatory revocation triggers include three reckless driving convictions within twenty-four months and two or more moving violations as a graduated driver, so the count and the time window both matter.

cards.front: Which crashes must be reported, how fast, and to whom?
cards.back: A crash causing injury or death to any person or property damage over one thousand dollars must be reported by the quickest means, oral or written, within five days to the local police department if it happens inside a municipality, and otherwise to the county sheriff or the nearest State Police office.

cards.front: What does the Driver License Compact do with out-of-state violations?
cards.back: Under the Driver License Compact, traffic violations in other states become part of your West Virginia record with points assessed when warranted, an out-of-state conviction that is grounds for suspension or revocation can suspend or revoke your West Virginia license, and other states may restrict your privilege to drive there.

cards.front: What does the Non-Resident Violator Compact allow, and what does each state agree to?
cards.back: Under the Non-Resident Violator Compact a driver may accept a citation for certain violations and continue on, and each member state agrees to suspend its own citizens who fail to comply with the terms of a violation committed in another state.

cards.front: What happens when you fail to appear or comply with a court order?
cards.back: Municipal, magistrate and circuit courts must notify the DMV when you fail to appear or fail to comply with any ticket, court order or decision, even a non-traffic matter, and the DMV suspends your license until you prove compliance and pay all penalty fees.

cards.front: What else must the DMV suspend a license for?
cards.back: State law also requires the DMV to suspend your driver's license if you fail to maintain child support payment obligations, so tickets and citations should be handled promptly.

cards.front: How are suspension, revocation and reinstatement transactions handled?
cards.back: All suspension, revocation and reinstatement transactions are handled in person at the Division of Motor Vehicles in Charleston, by mail to its post office box, or online through the DMV self-service site.

cards.front: What can you check or buy through DMV online services?
cards.back: The DMV Online Services page lets you check your license status, your total points and your commercial medical certification date, view and buy a driving record for twelve dollars and fifty cents, and pay license reinstatement fees.

cards.front: What triggers the crash-reporting duty, and how fast must you report?
cards.back: The crash-reporting duty is triggered by injury, death or property damage over one thousand dollars, and the report is due within five days to the local police inside a municipality or otherwise to the sheriff or State Police.

cards.front: How do the Driver License Compact and the Non-Resident Violator Compact differ?
cards.back: The Driver License Compact brings out-of-state convictions and points onto your record, while the Non-Resident Violator Compact lets you accept a citation and drive on but has your home state suspend you if you fail to comply.

cards.front: Which court and support failures lead to suspension?
cards.back: Failing to appear or comply with any court ticket or order, even a non-traffic one, and failing to maintain child support both lead the DMV to suspend the license.

decks.module: Fitness to drive and school attendance

cards.front: Who is responsible for a driver's actions, and what must a license holder know?
cards.back: The privilege to drive carries many responsibilities, you and only you are responsible for your actions, and a license holder must know the requirements that keep the privilege of driving in West Virginia.

cards.front: What happens to a minor's license when the school reports excessive absences?
cards.back: If your school notifies the DMV that you are not attending or have excessive unexcused absences, the DMV restricts your license to work, medical, educational and religious purposes until you turn eighteen or present a reinstatement authorization form from the school and pay the reinstatement fee.

cards.front: How do you refer an unsafe family member to the DMV, and who else may report?
cards.back: To refer an immediate family member who can no longer drive safely, write a detailed explanation to the DMV Medical Section giving the person's name, address, date of birth and license number if possible, and law enforcement or the person's physician may also submit such information.

cards.front: What may the DMV do after an unsafe-driver referral?
cards.back: After an unsafe-driver referral the DMV may reexamine the person's driving skills or request updated medical information from the doctor, and may then issue a restricted license or revoke the driving privilege for everyone's safety.

cards.front: When may you be required to retest, and what if you refuse?
cards.back: You may be required to take a medical, written or driving examination when the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles has good cause to believe you are incompetent or otherwise not qualified, the result may be suspension, revocation or a restricted license, and refusing the examination is itself grounds for suspension or revocation.

cards.front: How does a referral lead to re-examination, and what does refusing it cause?
cards.back: A referral about an unsafe family member can lead the DMV to reexamine that driver, and refusing a required re-examination is by itself grounds for suspension or revocation.
